speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin; has your feeding pattern and urine output changed since you started looking yellow? REQUEST TEST: Total_Bilirubin, Direct_Bilirubin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show a total bilirubin of 16.1 mg/dL with a normal direct fraction of 0.7 mg/dL, confirming significant unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Given your age, have you noticed any excessive sleepiness, poor feeding, or high-pitched crying? REQUEST IMAGES: Head_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; with a total bilirubin of 16.1 mg/dL at two weeks of age in a term infant who is exclusively breastfed, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of breast milk jaundice. Have you noticed any weight loss or signs of dehydration despite the weight gain? Also, is the stool dark green/black or has it turned pale/gray?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast Milk Jaundice. The combination of a term infant, exclusive breastfeeding, and significant unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia (Total 16.1, Direct 0.7) without signs of biliary obstruction or hemolysis is consistent with this diagnosis. The family history of sibling liver surgery is noted but less likely to explain this specific pattern of isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in a well-appearing 2-week-old.
